messages.text: Is the included power supply actually reliable?

**Yes — and it's genuinely over-spec'd for this job.**

The included **MEANWELL LRS-350-12** (350 W / 29 A, UL/CE/UKCA certified) is feeding a miner that draws **~100 W at full speed**. That's roughly **30% of its rated cap····** — industrial supplies running that lightly run cool, quiet, and last a very long time.

Why that matters:

- **Cheap bundled bricks** (~99–124 W) are already maxed out powering a ~100 W load — running at 100%+ 24/7 is how PSUs fail, and a failing PSU can take the miner with it
- The M. **loafs** — it never even breaks a sweat at stock settings
- It's the **same supply** used in extreme overclock research runs pushing well past 6 TH/s — so there's real headroom if you ever want to push the firmware later
- **UL/CE/UKCA certified** — not a no-name brick

Short version: it's a proper industrial power supply bundled with a ~100 W miner. That's the right way to do it.
what power supply comes with the miner if you don't get the overclocking bundle?

The NerdQaxe++ Rev 6.1 **only comes one way** — the **MEANWELL LRS-350-12 (350 W / 29 A)** is included in the box as standard. There's no separate "overclocking bundle" or base version without it.

What's in the box:
- The R. 6.1 unit
- **MEANWELL LRS-350-12** PSU
- 3D-printed BSB stand

That's it — one SKU, PSU always included. If you've seen a listing suggesting otherwise, it may be a different seller's version. Want me to check the live store for any current variants?
